claims.text: 11 July 1944 White House meeting of party leaders with Roosevelt recommended Truman; Roosevelt: 'Bob, I think you and everyone else here want Truman'; a note naming Truman and Douglas followed; 19 July call to Hannegan's suite: refusing would 'break up the Democratic Party in the middle of a war'.
Roosevelt sent Wallace to China and the Soviet Union in May 1944; Wallace wrote that Roosevelt 'wanted to ditch me as noiselessly as possible'.

20 July 1944: during the Wallace demonstration Jackson recognized Mayor David Lawrence, who moved adjournment; Jackson ruled 'the ayes have it'; Truman nominated 21 July (first ballot Wallace 429.5, Truman 319.5).
September 1946: Wallace criticized Truman's foreign policy in a speech at Madison Square Garden and was forced to resign as Secretary of Commerce.
